source.title: Infants selectively encode the goal object of an actor's reach

confidence_rationale: Landmark, heavily replicated infant-cognition result (>1600 citations) establishing that the goal of another agent's action is encoded as a primitive distinct from the physical movement that realises it. Directly grounds MECH-129's prerequisite (a) other-agent goal modelling and discriminant (1) what the other's goal is. Mapping is moderate-high: it evidences that goal-representation is separable from sensorimotor/contact representation -- which is exactly the architectural separation MECH-129 asserts -- but it shows goal-OBJECT encoding, not goal-OBSTRUCTION, so it grounds the substrate of harm-to-agency without directly demonstrating the harm signal itself.
failure_signatures: The effect is weaker at 5 months and absent for inanimate agents (an object of the same dimensions touching the toy), so the goal-encoding primitive is not a generic spatial-association mechanism -- it is gated on agency cues, which means a REE harm-to-agency signal computed over trajectory pairs must itself be gated on an agency/OTHER_SELFLIKE detector or it will fire on passive dynamics.

Goal-object encoding alone does not encode whether one's own action obstructs that goal (discriminant 2) -- Woodward shows the goal is represented, not that interference with it is registered as a cost.

mapping.source_claim_statement: By 6-9 months, infants encode an actor's reach in terms of the goal object grasped rather than the spatial path travelled; this selectivity is present for human (agentive) reaches but not for inanimate objects of matched dimensions.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-129 requires other-agent goal modelling -- the other's goal represented as a primitive in shared state (their z_goal) -- as the substrate for a goal-interference (harm-to-agency) signal. Woodward shows this primitive is real and early-developing in biological agents and, crucially, that it is represented separately from the sensorimotor trajectory. This is the developmental grounding for MECH-129's core architectural claim that harm-to-agency (over represented goals) is a distinct signal type from harm-to-agent (over self sensorimotor signals).
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paradigm demonstrates goal-OBJECT encoding, not goal-OBSTRUCTION detection: it grounds that goals of others are represented (MECH-129 prerequisite a / discriminant 1) but is silent on whether thwarting that goal is registered as a relational cost (discriminants 2-4, the actual harm-to-agency signal). It is also human-infant looking-time behaviour, not a mechanism for the interference computation over trajectory pairs that MECH-129 specifies.
mapping.source_context: Human infant visual-habituation studies (5-9 months), object-directed reaching events

confidence_components.notes: Source quality very high (canonical, replicated across labs and ages). Mapping fidelity good for the goal-representation substrate, partial for the harm signal. Transfer risk moderate: infant looking-time to REE computational substrate, and goal-object vs goal-obstruction gap.
